The scope of the role includes the development of new transmission stations and circuits and the refurbishment and upgrade of existing transmission stations and circuits. Strong collaboration and relationship building skills with the ability to effectively engage with other areas, companies and stakeholders, acknowledging different perspectives respectfully. review_candidates.company: EOSE - European Observatoire of Sport and Employment
review_candidates.description: The European Observatoire of Sport and Employment (EOSE) is looking for an experienced professional to join our team and contribute to the delivery and further development of our activities in the sport sector across Europe and internationally. The role covers a broad range of activities, including EU-funded projects, communication and marketing, research, publications, events, stakeholder relations and organisational development. The successful candidate will need to manage several priorities at the same time and be comfortable moving between different types of tasks according to EOSE’s needs. We are looking for someone who is comfortable with autonomy, adaptable, well organised and willing to take responsibility across different areas of work. > ABOUT EOSE: EOSE is a not-for-profit European Civil Society Organisation registered in France, bringing together a wide network of members, partners and stakeholders across Europe and beyond. Our ambition is to help the sport and physical activity sector realise its full potential and contribution to society, including in areas such as health and wellbeing, social inclusion, education, tourism, economic activity and employment. Achieving this potential requires paid professionals and volunteers with the right skills, competences and support to perform their roles effectively. EOSE’s mission is to facilitate and support the development of the sport workforce, bringing education and employment closer together and helping ensure that people working and volunteering in sport have the competences required by the sector. A central part of our role is to act as a facilitator between stakeholders, connecting sport employers, international, European and national sport federations, sport clubs and other sport organisations with education and training providers, public authorities, policymakers and other relevant actors. We also aim to connect needs and realities identified at local and national level with European policies, developments and opportunities. Our work evolves according to the needs of the sector, the expectations of sport stakeholders and developments in EU policies related to sport, education, youth and employment. Areas of activity include, for example, sport employment and workforce development, volunteering in sport, sport for development, dual careers, education and training, skills development, gender equality, safeguarding and digitalisation. Find out more: www.eose.org > MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES: As part of the EOSE team, the successful candidate will: Coordinate and manage EU-funded projects including planning, partner coordination, delivery of outputs, monitoring of deadlines and reporting requirements. Lead the development of new EU projects and funding applications , including identifying opportunities, developing ideas, building partnerships and preparing proposals. Undertake and coordinate research and consultation activities , including surveys, desk research, interviews, stakeholder consultation, analysis and reporting. Manage and produce communication activities and content , including social media, newsletters, website content, presentations and publications. Develop and maintain relationships with EOSE members, project partners and stakeholders , including sport organisations, public authorities, research centres, social partners and education and training providers. Plan and deliver meetings, workshops, seminars and events , both online and face-to-face. Contribute to the day-to-day administrative and financial management of projects and the wider organisation. Contribute to new ideas, partnerships and initiatives responding to emerging needs and opportunities in the sport sector, as well as to the wider development of EOSE. > ABOUT YOU > ABOUT YOU: We are looking for someone with at least 5 years of relevant professional experience , gained within the sport sector and/or in positions directly related to the main responsibilities of this role. You should have experience in project coordination or project management, ideally involving European or international collaborative projects, together with a good understanding of the European environment, EU programmes and relevant policy developments. You will also need: Excellent written and spoken English. Strong communication and writing skills. Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage several projects, activities and deadlines simultaneously. The ability to work autonomously in a remote environment while collaborating effectively as part of an international team. Strong digital confidence, including online collaboration tools and the ability to adapt quickly to new technologies. The ability to use AI-enabled tools appropriately and responsibly to support research, communication, organisation and day-to-day productivity. A genuine interest in and motivation to contribute to the sport sector. Willingness and availability to travel regularly in Europe and occasionally internationally. Experience in one or more of the following would be an advantage: direct professional experience in the sport sector preparation and implementation of EU funding applications research and data collection communication and digital content event organisation education and training development and/or delivery additional European languages market analysis, business development, product or service development. Previous involvement in sport as an athlete, coach, volunteer, official, employee, administrator or board member would also be welcomed. > WHAT WE OFFER > WHAT WE OFFER: EOSE offers an international, collaborative and stimulating working environment, with exposure to a wide range of projects, topics, organisations and stakeholders across Europe and beyond. The role offers a high degree of autonomy and the opportunity to take responsibility across different areas of work. EOSE places strong importance on the wellbeing, professional development and working conditions of its staff and aims to provide a supportive and flexible working environment. The position will be full-time and remote, with regular travel associated with projects, meetings and events. EOSE welcomes applications from candidates based across Europe. Employment arrangements, remuneration and detailed conditions will be discussed during the recruitment process and agreed according to the successful candidate’s profile, responsibilities and country of employment, in line with applicable national requirements. > EQUALITY AND INCLUSION EOSE is committed to equal opportunities and an inclusive working environment. We welcome applications from suitably qualified candidates regardless of gender, age, disability, or other personal characteristics. Candidates requiring adjustments during the recruitment process are encouraged to let us know. > HOW TO APPLY: Please submit to Mr Aurélien Favre, EOSE Executive Director, using eosesec@eose.org : Your CV A motivation letter in English explaining your interest in the role, your relevant experience and the contribution you believe you could make to EOSE. >>> Application deadline: 15 November 2026 (midnight, Paris/Brussels time) <<< Shortlisted candidates will be invited to an initial online interview in December 2026, with a possible subsequent online or face-to-face meeting. Preferred starting date: as early as possible during the first quarter of 2027, taking into account the successful candidate’s availability and notice period.

review_candidates.description: Description Job Title: Country Director - Kenya Location: Remote, Kenya (with regular travel within Kenya and to the UK) Salary: $65,000 - $80,000 p.a. full-time equivalent, dependent on experience. Salary is paid in USD Basis: Permanent. Full-time, part-time or flexible Eligibility: You must be eligible to work in Kenya The role We are looking for an experienced Country Director to lead our work in Kenya. Reporting to the Chief Growth Officer, you will be responsible for delivering the Raspberry Pi Foundation's strategy in Kenya, ensuring our programmes reach the educators and young people who stand to benefit most. You will have a strong track record of leading educational programmes in Kenya and will have established relationships across the sector. You will be responsible for scaling our operations in the country, managing a high-performing team, growing our network of partners, and deepening our impact with key stakeholders in the education ecosystem. We work hard to make sure that the Foundation is a place where everyone is supported to do the best work of their careers. We have a flexible and collaborative approach to all aspects of our work. If you're the right person for the job, we’ll make it work for you, and you can be confident that you’ll be joining an exceptional team of people who care about our mission and each other. Responsibilities Develop and implement strategies to increase the reach and impact of the Foundation's products in Kenya. Develop and manage strategic relationships with mission-aligned partners including county and national government. Lead engagement with senior education stakeholders in Kenya, ensuring the Foundation understands and is influencing the policy environment and is proactively engaging with relevant networks and organisations. Ensure that all programmes and partnerships have clear monitoring and evaluation plans. Use data and feedback to ensure quality and identify areas for improvement. Work collaboratively with colleagues across the Foundation to develop and improve educational products for Kenyan educators and young people, and share learnings. Build, lead, and manage a highly skilled team, providing them with the clarity and support to enable them to do great work. Ensure that all programmes and partnerships implement our commitments to accessibility, inclusion, and safeguarding, prioritising impact for underserved and educationally disadvantaged young people and communities. Manage the Kenya budget and report on progress to key funders, working in collaboration with the Chief Growth Officer. As a member of the Leadership team, contribute to the strategic direction, culture, and values of the organisation. Represent the Raspberry Pi Foundation externally. Experience and personal attributes We recognise that everyone has the potential for growth. We welcome applications from candidates who can demonstrate that they have some, but not necessarily all, of the experience and personal attributes listed here. A significant track record of leading educational programmes at scale within Kenya. Experience developing and managing high-value strategic partnerships with governments, NGOs, and other mission-aligned organisations. Existing relationships with senior government officials and wider education stakeholders in Kenya. An experienced senior manager and leader with a proven ability to build diverse teams and support them to do great work. Ideally, you will have experience managing remote and geographically dispersed teams. A track record of delivering impactful learning experiences, products, and programs, ideally focused on young people, alongside a strong understanding of how to measure learner success, demonstrate program impact and use data to improve what we do. A proven ability to leverage thought leadership, advocacy, and policy influence to drive systemic change. A deep and demonstrable commitment to diversity and inclusion, and experience translating that commitment into programme design, delivery, and evaluation. Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the credibility and presence to represent the Foundation at senior levels externally. A genuine commitment to the Foundation's mission to enable all young people to realise their full potential through the power of computing and AI. About Us The Raspberry Pi Foundation is an independent charity with a global mission to enable all young people to realise their full potential through the power of computing and digital technologies. We empower schools to teach computer science and AI literacy through free curricula, classroom resources, purpose built software tools, and professional development for teachers. We inspire young people to become tech creators through the world's largest networks of coding clubs. We undertake original research that informs our work and which we use to advance the field of computer science education more broadly. All of our resources and learning experiences are available for anyone to use at no cost. We are particularly focused on creating opportunities for young people who experience educational disadvantage and those who come from backgrounds traditionally underrepresented in technology industries. Over the past decade, we have supported hundreds of thousands of educators and tens of millions of students. We have teams in six countries (India, Ireland, Kenya, South Africa, the UK and US) and partnerships with mission-aligned non-profit organisations in over 60 countries. We are at the forefront of the global educational movement to expand access to computer science education and AI literacy. You can learn more about our work in our latest Annual Report. Benefits In addition to competitive salaries, we offer a wide range of benefits for all of our colleagues. Paid time off. In addition to public holidays, full-time employees in Kenya receive 21 days of paid annual leave, plus 3 additional days of paid leave for the company-wide closure at the end of each year. Pension. We provide an 8% employer contribution on top of your minimum 4% employee contribution. Private healthcare. We provide comprehensive private healthcare for all employees and their legal spouse and up to 3 dependents through CIC. This includes cover for dental and vision. Flexible working. We have clear policies to provide flexibility over when and where you work, helping you balance work responsibilities with the rest of your life. Life assurance and WIBA/GPA We provide life assurance and Group Personal Accident Insurance to provide peace of mind for you and your family. Investing in learning and development. We invest in your growth and development, including through access to learning resources and training, with dedicated time for all employees. Timetable for applications Closing date: 12 October 2026, 9.00am EAT Phone screen: Week commencing 19 October 2026 First interview: Week commencing 2 November 2026 Second interview: Week commencing 9 November 2026 Our recruitment process All of our workplaces are inclusive spaces where we want people to feel respected, valued, and able to do their best work. We are committed to building teams that bring together people with a broad range of backgrounds, skills, and perspectives. That starts with our recruitment process. Here's What You Can Expect As part of your application, you will be asked to respond to a small number of questions that we will use to screen your eligibility for the role. You will also be asked to provide your cv. Eligible applications will be reviewed by our recruitment team and the hiring manager. We review all applications for authenticity. While we embrace the use of AI tools to assist you, all content must genuinely represent your own work, and have been reviewed and personalised by you. A small number of candidates will be invited to a phone call with the hiring manager. The purpose of this call is to check our understanding of your application and to answer any questions you have. We normally have two interviews, which may take place in-person. Interviews will be with the hiring manager and at least one other colleague. You will usually be asked to undertake a work-based assessment in advance of your interviews. This will be an opportunity for you to show how you would perform some part of the role. You will be given advance notice and clear instructions. If you have any questions about or feel that you need any adjustments to the recruitment process, including adjustments for neurodiversity, please contact our People and Culture team at recruitment@raspberrypi.org. We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people, and we expect all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. Everyone appointed to a role at the Foundation will be required to undergo a background check to confirm that you are a suitable person to work with children. Further background checks will be made at regular intervals thereafter.

Position Title: Business Support Associate - Supply Chain Type of Contract: Fixed term Grade: GS – 6 Duty Station: Phnom Penh, Cambodia Duration: One year ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT: The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) Cambodia works with government, development, and humanitarian partners to improve food security, nutrition, and resilience across the country. Reporting to the Deputy Country Director or designated supervisor, the Business Support Associate - Supply Chain provides operational and administrative support across procurement, logistics, contracting, and inventory management activities. The position contributes to the efficient, compliant, and cost-effective delivery of goods and services, while supporting day-to-day coordination with suppliers, service providers, and internal stakeholders. JOB PURPOSE: To provide specialized operational, administrative, and coordination support across supply chain management functions, including procurement, contracting, logistics, inventory management, and vendor relations, ensuring the efficient and compliant delivery of goods and services in support of programme implementation and organizational objectives. BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF ASSIGNMENT: The World Food Programme (WFP) Cambodia is implementing its Country Strategic Plan (CSP) through integrated programme and operational support functions that enable efficient, accountable and sustainable delivery of assistance. Within this context, the Business Support Associate (Supply Chain) contributes to the effective planning, coordination and monitoring of supply chain activities that support programme implementation and partnership engagement across the Country Office. The incumbent provides specialized business support and coordination across supply chain functions, including procurement coordination, inventory oversight, transport management, performance monitoring and stakeholder engagement. The position supports data-driven decision-making, compliance, risk management and continuous improvement initiatives to strengthen operational efficiency and ensure effective delivery of CSP priorities. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES (not all-inclusive, nor exhaustive): Coordinate end-to-end supply chain operations, including procurement, contracting, logistics, warehousing, inventory management, and distribution activities to ensure timely and cost-effective delivery of goods and services. Manage sourcing and vendor engagement, including market assessments, supplier selection, tendering processes, contract preparation, performance monitoring, and resolution of operational issues. Oversee the movement, storage, and control of goods and supplies, ensuring accurate inventory records, shipment tracking, customs clearance, and compliance with operational procedures. Maintain supply chain information and reporting systems, analyze operational data, and prepare reports to support planning, performance monitoring, compliance, and informed decision-making. Support financial and operational planning, including budget monitoring, resource management, audit readiness, risk mitigation, and adherence to organizational policies and procedures. Build and maintain effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders, supervise support staff as required, and contribute to emergency preparedness, response activities, and continuous process improvement. Experience in supply and demand planning, inventory management, warehousing, transportation, and end-to-end supply chain operations. Experience conducting market assessments, supplier evaluations, sourcing activities, contract administration, and vendor performance management. Experience using ERP systems or similar (e.g., SAP/WINGS) and reporting tools for transaction processing, operational monitoring, and reporting. Experience in budget monitoring, data analysis, KPI tracking, and preparation of management reports to support decision-making and performance improvement.
